item.text:
**Bottom Line**
3B.7 is mostly negative for Tshisekedi in 2024. I found some positive conflict-mitigation steps, especially local peace agreements and ceasefire diplomacy, but not a convincing record of systematic protection for women, children, minorities, and other vulnerable groups from targeted violence, displacement, or neglect. The strongest counterevidence is continued civilian harm, mass displacement, prison sexual violence, and ongoing abuses by security forces and militias.

**Accepted Claims**
- **DR Congo: Investigate Prison Deaths, Sexual Violence** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-09-06** | [source](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/06/dr-congo-investigate-prison-deaths-sexual-violence)  
  HRW says authorities should investigate the Makala prison disaster and provide a transparent account, indicating that vulnerable detainees were not protected from catastrophic abuse in custody.  
  **IDs:** `3B.7`, `3B.1`, `3B.4`

- **More than 260 women sexually assaulted during Congo prison break, UN report shows** | **Reuters** | **2024-09-12** | [source](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/More-than-260-women-sexually-assaulted-during-Congo-prison-break-UN-reports-shows-47860482/)  
  Reuters reports prison guards used live fire during the Makala escape attempt, killing at least 129 people, and that more than 260 female inmates were sexually assaulted. This is severe evidence of state failure to protect vulnerable women in custody.  
  **IDs:** `3B.7`, `3B.1`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`

- **World Report 2024: Democratic Republic of Congo** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024** | [source](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/democratic-republic-congo)  
  HRW says government forces killed dozens of civilians during enforcement of a protest ban in Goma, while repression against journalists, activists, critics, and opposition members continued. That supports a finding that vulnerable groups were not reliably protected from targeted or systematic abuse.  
  **IDs:** `3B.7`, `3B.5`, `3B.2`, `3B.1`, `3B.4`

- **DRC President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-09-30** | [source](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/)  
  Amnesty says the government failed to prevent and punish sexual violence and attacks against civilians and allowed security forces and affiliated militias to continue targeting civilians. This is strong evidence against systematic protection of vulnerable groups.  
  **IDs:** `3B.7`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.4`

- **DRC President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-06-24** | [source](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/)  
  Amnesty says security forces and affiliated militias continued to target civilians and that little progress had been made on prior human-rights pledges. This is broad negative evidence for women, children, and vulnerable communities.  
  **IDs:** `3B.7`, `3B.2`, `3B.1`

- **Around 20 civilians killed in Congo attack, army and rebels trade blame** | **Reuters** | **2024-01-25** | [source](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/around-20-civilians-killed-in-congo-attack-army-and-rebels-trade-blame-3283402)  
  Reuters reported around 20 civilians were killed in Mweso, including displacement-linked violence in an already vulnerable area. This is negative evidence that civilians were still exposed to lethal harm despite the government’s stated peace efforts.  
  **IDs:** `3B.7`, `3B.1`, `2B.7`

- **Airstrike kills nine at displacement camp** | **Reuters** | **2024-05-03** | [source](https://www.yahoo.com/news/airstrike-kills-nine-displacement-camp-110342393.html)  
  Reuters reported nine civilians, including seven children, were killed in a strike on a displacement camp near Goma. This is direct evidence of failure to protect displaced children and other vulnerable civilians.  
  **IDs:** `3B.7`, `3B.1`, `2B.4`

- **Les Téké et les Yaka s’engagent à mettre fin aux hostilités dans l’ouest de la RDC** | **Présidence RDC** | **2024-04-06** | [source](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/les_teke_et_les_yaka_sengagent_a_mettre_fin_aux_hostilites_dans_louest_de_la_rdc)  
  Tshisekedi presided over a local peace agreement in western DRC where Téké and Yaka representatives committed to dialogue, mediation, and arbitration. This is the clearest positive evidence that he sometimes supported intercommunal de-escalation.  
  **IDs:** `3B.7`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`

- **Crise sécuritaire dans l’Est de la RDC: les présidents Félix Tshisekedi et João Lourenço appellent au respect du cessez-le-feu** | **Présidence RDC** | **2024-08-12** | [source](https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/crise_securitaire_dans_lest_de_la_rdc_les_presidents_felix_tshisekedi_et_joao_lourenco_appellent_au_respect_du_cessez_le_feu)  
  Tshisekedi backed the Luanda process, welcomed the 4 August ceasefire, and said his government was available for next steps. This is positive but limited evidence of protecting vulnerable civilians through de-escalation rather than force.  
  **IDs:** `3B.7`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`

- **Collective effort essential to get DR Congo on firm path to peace** | **UN Office at Geneva** | **2024-09-30** | [source](https://www.ungeneva.org/en/news-media/news/2024/09/98156/collective-effort-essential-get-dr-congo-firm-path-peace)  
  The UN said fighting had decreased after the 30 July ceasefire and a dialogue framework was active under Angolan mediation. This supports a limited positive reading, but only for temporary reduction in violence, not durable protection of vulnerable groups.  
  **IDs:** `3B.7`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`

**Search Gap**
I found no strong evidence that Tshisekedi’s government systematically protected vulnerable groups across 2024. The positive items are mostly peace-process and ceasefire signals; the negative record still includes killings, displacement, prison sexual violence, repression, and ongoing militia and security-force abuse.
